title: Saints Kool-Aid McKinstry named NFC Defensive Player of the Week, Chase Young returns to practice - NewsBreak
text:
By Sara Palczewski ,
4 hours ago
METAIRIE, La. (Louisiana First) — New Orleans Saints defensive end Chase Young officially returned to practice Wednesday after missing the first five games of the year with a calf injury. Young was limited.
Saints head coach Kellen Moore said there’s optimism with him playing Sunday and called Wednesday a good step.
If Young returns Sunday, he’ll be rejoining a unit with the NFC Defensive Player of the Week, Kool-Aid McKinstry. McKistry hauled in his first two career interceptions Sunday against the New York Giants while also having three passes defended and four total tackles to take home his first conference honors.
Sunday was arguably the 2024 second-round pick’s best performance and will only aid in his development.
“I mean, Kool-Aid’s… like you said, he’s a young player,” Moore said. “He’s still got a lot of growth opportunities, just like some of these other guys. He’s taken some really good steps. I think having two interceptions, being the NFC Defensive Player of the Week, there’s some confidence, I think, that comes out of that. You can see him with a little bit of that confidence, that swagger coming out of him. We obviously think highly of him. We think he’s gonna be a tremendous corner for us for a long time. He’s going to continue to progress really well.”
“I’m the type of guy, I’m a humble guy, man,” McKinstry said. “I keep my head down. I work. I stay coachable, and that’s what I do. So that’s me. Don’t no award change me. I am who I am.”
